notes:
Account summary
- Enterprise bank evaluating Redwood Private for internal knowledge + analyst workflows. Very sensitive to security posture, operational controls, and change management.
- Core ask: Private deployment in their AWS VPC (no public egress from inference pods; allowlisted control-plane endpoints only). Secondary: Dedicated capacity as interim bridge if Private lead time slips.

Primary contacts
- Platform Engineering lead ("internal AI platform"), Security Architecture, and SRE manager. Procurement engaged informally (asking for order-of-magnitude pricing + support tier).

Use cases / workload
- Document search + summarization over internal policies and regulatory docs.
- Analyst assistant that may do tool-calling (internal search + retrieval + summarization). Mix of streaming and non-streaming.
- Early sizing shared verbally: 300–800 RPS burst across business hours, but expects heavy concurrency on a few workflows (morning market open). Wants predictable p95.

Performance requirements (stated)
- "We can live with slightly higher p50, but p95 needs to be stable." Target: p95 < 450ms time-to-first-token for typical chat responses; avoid p99 spikes during concurrency.
- Wants throughput/cost story in tokens/sec/GPU and concrete guidance for batch/queue settings. Explicit concern: tuning profiles that increase throughput but create tail-latency blowups.

Security + compliance requirements
- SSO/SAML for Console; strict RBAC for config changes.
- Audit logging: must capture who changed what (especially runtime config and hardware profile overrides), and retain logs >= 1 year.
- KMS integration (customer-managed keys). Prefers HSM-backed CMK.
- Data residency: US regions only. No cross-region fallback unless explicitly approved.
- Retention controls: request/response logging must be configurable/off by default; metrics only is acceptable.

Private deployment architecture asks / questions
- Override model: they want to keep Redwood-provided defaults but allow per-cluster and per-namespace overrides for a small set of knobs.
- Specific questions on hardware tuning profiles pack:
  - "Can we pin the H100 profile and freeze it across upgrades?" (They do quarterly change windows.)
  - "If we override any profile knobs, do we still get support?" They want a clear support boundary.
  - "What’s the override precedence?" (fleet defaults vs Helm values vs env vars vs per-route config). Asked for a single canonical reference.
  - "How do we validate what’s actually running?" Requested a way to dump effective runtime config for audit and troubleshooting.
  - "Can we disable experimental profiles by policy?" (They referenced B200 bring-up concerns; want an explicit opt-in flag.)

Observability / operations asks
- Wants dashboards segmented by hardware profile selection (H100 vs others) and ability to correlate tail latency regressions to profile changes.
- Requested explicit rollback semantics:
  - ability to revert to previous profile pack version quickly
  - ability to disable profile selection and run runtime defaults
  - ability to scope rollback to a pool/cluster (not global)
- Wants alert thresholds and playbooks: what metrics trip rollback, and who’s on point (their SRE vs Redwood support).

Recent activity timeline
- 2025-11-06: Discovery call (Platform Eng + Security). They indicated Private is the only acceptable long-term option.
- 2025-11-20: Security intake: asked for SOC2/ISO scope, encryption details, audit log schema, and data retention defaults.
- 2025-12-09: Technical deep dive with SE (Diego). Focused on deployment topology and override controls.
- 2026-01-16: Follow-up email thread about profile overrides and whether they can lock a profile version across runtime upgrades.
- 2026-02-11: Workshop request from their SRE: "show us rollback in <15 minutes" + what to monitor during canary.

What they care about / buying criteria
- Strong operational guardrails (canary + rollback), clear override order, and debuggability.
- Documentation must separate expected behavior vs guarantees (they’re sensitive to vendor overpromising).
- Support model: wants a named escalation path during rollout.

Proposed Redwood response (draft)
- Recommend starting with H100 tuned profile in balanced mode; require explicit opt-in for throughput-first.
- Provide a compatibility/versioning approach: pin profile pack version, with runtime startup logging compatibility matrix.
- Provide override guide via Helm values (Private) + policy to disallow env var overrides in prod.
- Provide observability pack: metrics for selected profile + override source; dashboard panels for tail latency.
- Provide staged rollout runbook: canary in one cluster, then expand by pool; rollback triggers based on p95/p99 + error/OOM rate.

Open questions
- Confirm their exact GPU fleet (H100 SXM vs PCIe; any MIG usage). If MIG is in scope, clarify whether profile applies per-device or per-node.
- Clarify whether they will allow a single dedicated test pool to run experimental B200 later (opt-in only).

Internal tags
- Notes to self: very sensitive to change-control language. Avoid words like "guarantee". Emphasize safe-by-default + measurable + reversible.
- Consider pulling in SRE sponsor (Sean Gallagher) for the rollout readiness session; also loop in runtime config owner (Benji Okafor) if they push on override precedence details.
